references.text: "His tent is in Salem, his dwelling place on Zion." Here Salem is identified with Jerusalem, linking Melchizedek's kingdom to the place that later became God's holy city.

"The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek." This verse prophesies an eternal priesthood after the order of Melchizedek, pointing forward to the Messiah.
In Hebrews, Jesus is described as a priest after the order of Melchizedek, which directly connects his priesthood to Melchizedek in Genesis 14.
Jesus has gone before us as our forerunner, having become high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
Hebrews 7:1-10 discusses Melchizedek as king of Salem and priest of God Most High, showing how his priesthood serves as a pattern for Christ's eternal priesthood.
Hebrews confirms and expands upon the historical event and identity of the person from Genesis, forming the basis for the typological interpretation of Melchizedek.
